Definition: from G4263; relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem:--sheep (market).
BiblicalUsage: Probatikos means relating to sheep, and John uses it once, for the sheep gate at Jerusalem. There is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, called Bethesda, where the sick lay waiting for the moving of the water.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sheep gate led the sheep to slaughter, and the pool beside it is where the Good Shepherd found the man no one else would heal.
